job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

response.passage: In a bustling classroom in Delhi, Mr. Sharma discussed the Indian Constitution with his students, Rohan and Meera. 'The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949,' Mr. Sharma explained, pointing to a map of India. Rohan asked, 'Sir, did Dr. Ambedkar write it alone?' Mr. Sharma smiled, 'No, he led a Drafting Committee of seven members. Because the committee members debated extensively, the document reflects diverse viewpoints.' Meera added, 'I read that the Preamble starts with We the People.' Mr. Sharma nodded, 'Exactly. That phrase signifies that the power of the state rests with the citizens, not the rulers. In 1950, the Constitution officially came into force, marking a new era for our democracy. It is a living document, meaning it adapts to the changing needs of society.' Rohan looked at the map. 'So, does the Constitution only apply to people living in Delhi?' Mr. Sharma laughed gently, 'Not at all, Rohan. It applies to every citizen across the entire nation, regardless of where they live.'
response.summary: Mr. Sharma explains the origins and nature of the Indian Constitution to his students. He clarifies that the document was a collaborative effort and emphasizes that it applies to all citizens of India.
